title: Density part of localized relative normalization
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian quasi-separated scheme whose local rings are integrally closed [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $c:C\to S$ be quasi-compact, quasi-separated and smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $U\subset S$ be open, $P\to C_U=c^{-1}(U)$ a finite etale scheme [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and $s\in S$. Put $f:P\to C_U\to C$, $L=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ with projection $l:L\to C$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $n:N=f.\mathrm{normalization}\times_C L\to L$, where relative normalization means integral closure of $\mathcal O_C$ in $f_*\mathcal O_P$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization].. Then the open n^{-1}(l^{-1}(C_U)) is dense in N.

proof.text: The integral-closure inclusion gives ker(f.toNormalization) = 0 (Mathlib Scheme.Hom.ker_toNormalization). Stalk localization is flat (Scheme.flat_fromSpecStalk), as are its two pullbacks. Apply the flat base-change tool via Mathlib IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.pullbackSnd to obtain a quasi-compact schematically dominant map k : P ×_M N → N. Its image is dense.

The two pullback identities and toNormalization_fromNormalization give k ≫ n ≫ l = pullback.fst ≫ f. The image of f lies in C_U, so range(k) lies in n^{-1}(l^{-1}(C_U)). A set containing a dense set is dense (Dense.mono).

lean.statement:
theorem stalk_normalization_dense_part {S C : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsIntegral S]
    (_hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (c : C ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact c] [QuasiSeparated c] [Smooth c]
    (U : S.Opens)
    (PA : (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.FiniteEtale)
    (s : S) :
    letI : IsFinite PA.obj.hom := PA.property
    letI : QuasiCompact (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (isPullback_morphismRestrict c U)
        (inferInstance : QuasiCompact U.ι)
    let f := PA.obj.hom ≫ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι
    let l := pullback.fst c (S.fromSpecStalk s)
    let n := pullback.snd f.fromNormalization l
    Dense (↑(n ⁻¹ᵁ (l ⁻¹ᵁ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U))) :
      Set (pullback f.fromNormalization l : Scheme.{u}))
